name: Panasonic EH-ST63
technology: Legacy ion delivery; warm/cool skincare tool.
research: The directly attributable Lab Muffin review is Panasonic-sponsored and discusses this exact older model. It explains ion mechanisms and points out controls missing from the clinical literature reviewed in 2018. It is expert commentary, not an EH-ST63 efficacy trial.
fit: Possible compatible vitamin-C ion use; no recovered exact-model clinical increment.
value: Legacy purchase only if much cheaper than ST99 and its battery/accessories remain sound. No verified eBay quote in this review.

name: Panasonic EH-ST99
technology: BOOST pretreatment plus ion MOIST/BRIGHT UP; heating/cooling; no RF or EMS.
research: The official regional catalogue reports HA5.7× and collagen5.0× relative to hand application. Legacy methods are less fully recovered than newer models. The earlier pasted peptide6.3× number remains unverified.
fit: A reasonable budget ion choice for compatible vitamin C. HA/collagen tests do not rank its effectiveness for niacinamide.
value: B value tier: budget Panasonic choice; pay for condition before headline output.
why: Lower reported HA uptake does not establish worse small-active clinical results than ST0A.

name: Panasonic EH-ST0A
technology: Upgraded BOOST head plus ion modes; heating/cooling; no RF or EMS.
research: Manufacturer n10 forearm comparison of BOOST+MOIST with hand application: HA8.0× and oligopeptide-1 9.3× in the outer skin barrier. Output1.6× versus ST99 is an engineering comparison. Neither result measures better acne/pigment outcomes from the user’s routine.
fit: Compatible vitamin-C ion protocol is the plausible use; the headline upgrade targets ingredients you rarely use.
value: B value tier: sensible Panasonic alternative, without proof that the ST99 premium helps your actives.
why: At $36 above the observed ST99, newer generation/condition can justify it; small-active efficacy alone cannot.

name: Panasonic EH-SS85 Ion Boost Multi EX
technology: Dedicated BOOST and ion delivery; EMS; warm/cool; no RF.
research: Manufacturer uptake tests: HA12×,n8; hydrolyzed collagen6.3×; vitamin C1.6×,n12,in BRIGHT UP. The ingredient,mode and cohort differ.

Manufacturer hydration evaluation,n10,measures three-hour hydration; four-week n26 half-face evaluation concerns dry fine lines with the full multimode course. It does not isolate increased vitamin-C delivery as the cause.
fit: My higher-budget pick for a dedicated compatible-vitamin-C delivery device. Its 12× HA claim is not your vitamin-C result.
value: C value tier at current price: better documentation than a compelling dollar-for-dollar upgrade.
why: Best-documented dedicated vitamin-C option in this source set; preference has low confidence for visible superiority. No matched head-to-head trial.

name: Panasonic EH-SM50 Ion Boost mask
technology: Hands-free mask/ion format.
research: Official HA comparisons report10× relative to a sheet mask alone and5.1× relative to manually applied serum. The baselines differ, so these numbers do not create a ranking against ST0A/SS85.
fit: Convenience and hydration rather than a demonstrated increment for your small active ingredients.
value: Do not pay extra for delivery efficacy; no verified eBay quote in this review.

name: Panasonic EH-SR85 Vitalift RF
technology: RF 3MHz with model-specific ion/EMS skincare functions.
research: Official product specifications support the feature combination. No adequately assessed exact-model matched-formula delivery study is established in this dossier. SS85 BOOST results cannot be transferred to this hardware.
fit: Consider only if RF tightening is an additional goal. Compare its RF evidence separately from ingredient delivery.
value: No verified eBay quote included. Dedicated RF assessment is available in the archive’s RF topic.

name: YA-MAN Photo Plus Shiny M18-YL
technology: Original DYHP/ion system with RF/EMS/LED.
research: August2022 manufacturer human tape-stripping assay,n10 men: M18-YL switched OFF versus DYHP, vitamin-C derivative VCPMG uptake about1.7× into stratum corneum. Exact model is explicitly identified on the later Neo page.
fit: More directly relevant to vitamin C than HA-only tests, but only the tested derivative/protocol; not a finished-serum clinical trial.
value: Potential older bargain only at a clearly low complete-unit price; no verified eBay quote in this review.
why: Evidence grade upgraded from D to C after recovering the original-model test footnote.

name: YA-MAN Photo Plus Shiny Neo YJFM18N
technology: DYHP/ion plus RF1–3MHz,EMS,LED; daily/weekly programs.
research: The widely advertised1.7× vitamin-C derivative tape-stripping test used original M18-YL, not Neo. A Neo n14 immediate subjective half-face evaluation reports perceived hydration/stimulation. It does not establish a clinically superior delivery effect.
fit: My value choice if you also explicitly want RF; no evidence-based reason to pay Deep Lift prices solely for niacinamide delivery.
value: B with a separate RF goal; C for delivery alone.
why: Extra features can add personal value, but this source set does not prove its RF or delivery superiority.

name: YA-MAN Photo Plus Deep Lift YJFA1T
technology: DYHP/ion and RF1–4MHz; EMS/LED.
research: Manufacturer forearm study,n10 men,one minute,aqueous ingredients,stratum-corneum measurement. Chart ratios are approximately1.7× vitamin-C derivative,1.4× tranexamic acid,1.7× niacinamide. These are total ratios, not an additional170% clinical benefit.
fit: Closest ingredient match to both your vitamin C and niacinamide, but not your finished formulas or clinical outcomes.
value: D for penetration-only value at $550+; an optional premium RF combination.
why: More relevant assay than HA marketing; insufficient evidence that it beats a $110 Pro in useful visible results.

name: YA-MAN Photo Plus Prestige S M20

research: Official specifications/marketing establish the technology package. No complete exact-model matched-product clinical delivery comparison was adequately recovered and reviewed here. Generic electroporation literature and the M18/Deep Lift tests cannot be counted as a trial of this model.
fit: No demonstrated advantage for your vitamin C/niacinamide and no evidence-based reason to boost your other three actives.
value: Premium delivery value is unsubstantiated. No verified model-specific eBay quote; price stays unknown rather than inferred from retail.
why: Premium generations must remain separate: a shared brand or pulse acronym does not establish equal waveforms, dose or efficacy.

research: Official international page claims vitamin-C derivative1.7×,niacinamide1.9×,TXA1.4× for NEB+DWHP. It also lists eight-week appearance improvements, but the readable summary lacks an adequate sample/control/protocol description for a clinical efficacy grade.
fit: Ingredients match the two plausible parts of your routine; opaque public methods limit confidence.
value: Poorly justified premium for delivery alone; no verified eBay quote.
why: The1.9× niacinamide claim is not proof of superiority to Deep Lift’s1.7×; assays are not standardized.

name: Medicube AGE-R Booster-H
technology: Older dedicated electroporation booster.
research: Four manufacturer reports were located: a four-week vitamin-C split-face comparison, acute vitamin-C appearance test,24-hour hydration test,and cream/dry-weather test. Read their methods/results below; all belong to Booster-H.
fit: The strongest located exact-model matched-vitamin-C clinical signal in the Medicube family, though small and biased. Does not validate your unknown vitamin-C formula.
value: Only attractive if appreciably cheaper than the $110 Pro and with a reliable battery; no verified current eBay quote.
why: Grade upgraded from U to C+ after reviewing the public reports. Study breadth does not remove manufacturer sponsorship or fixed-side bias.

name: Medicube AGE-R Booster Pro
technology: Booster electroporation; microcurrent,Derma Shot EMS,Air Shot dry electric microporation,LED/sonic; no RF tightening mode.
research: Hur et al.2023 exact-Pro trial:21 women in EP arm,four weeks,500ppm glutathione ampoule both sides,left-side device2min twice daily at level5. Preliminary pigment/brightness improvement; manufacturer authors,fixed side,no reported blinding,and unpaired between-side analyses.

Kwak et al.2023 exact-Pro trial:44 women split into22 MC and22 EMS users,two weeks,matched ampoule on both sides. Reports appearance/lifting changes, with similar bias/statistics limitations. This adds support for extra modes, not absorption.
fit: My best balanced paid purchase: low price plus some exact-model human evidence involving another small active. Benefit for your vitamin-C/niacinamide products remains an inference.
value: A value tier at about$110: my overall paid pick. Prefer it over Mini Plus if the roughly$33 premium is acceptable.
why: Clinical evidence is preliminary, not proof it beats Panasonic. Booster-H vitamin-C reports are contextual, not exact-Pro trials.

name: Medicube Mini Booster Pro
technology: Simpler electroporation booster with red/blue LED.
research: The advertised562% absorption summary does not expose enough ingredient/absolute-dose/method detail for a trustworthy clinical comparison. It must not be treated as the Mini Plus caffeine experiment.
fit: Lowest observed entry price, but weaker public evidence than Mini Plus/Pro.
value: A low-cost experiment; Mini Plus is the more evidence-informed simple-device pick for the small price difference.
why: Seller does not accept returns; account for that when comparing a new claim against a tested used Pro.

name: Medicube Mini Booster Pro Plus
technology: Distinct newer three-mode device: cleansing/definition/boost.
research: Report excerpt NCR-25501-PR065 identifies caffeine transport:15min sampling control16.6 vs test103.7µg/mL,6.25×;4hr ratio3.17×. The manufacturer identifies Mini Plus and TegoScience testing May8–June2,2025. Full skin model,n,settings and sampled compartment remain unavailable.
fit: My cheapest evidence-informed penetration-only experiment. Caffeine is a small molecule, but its result does not validate vitamin C or niacinamide.
value: A value tier; about$77 at the sampled sealed-claim offer.
why: 625% of control equals525% more, not625% more. Sampling time is not confirmed treatment duration.

name: Medicube Booster Pro X2
technology: Newer dual-head seven-mode booster; manufacturer expanded features/app.
research: The2× comparison concerns tested power density in W/cm² versus Pro. No recovered exact-X2 matched-vitamin-C/niacinamide trial establishes a stronger clinical result. Original Pro’s trials are not X2 trials.
fit: No evidence-based efficacy upgrade for your routine. Avoid making stronger exposure to tazarotene a purchasing goal.
value: Conditional A only for a verified authentic bargain; standard new-claim offer costs more without a demonstrated outcome advantage.
why: Do not let the unusually cheap new-other listing anchor the decision before verifying exact model/authenticity and returns.

name: ReFa BEAUTECH RAISE

research: Official product/FAQ describe the combination and instructions. No adequately assessed exact-device matched-formula clinical penetration increment was located. RF,sonic vibration and a pulse label are not proof of clinical sonophoresis or of better serum delivery.
fit: No clear reason to prefer this over lower-priced alternatives for your active routine.
value: Delivery value remains uncertain; no verified eBay quote in this review.

name: ARTISTIC&CO Dr.Arrivo Zeus II
technology: Legacy proprietary pulse beauty device; exact regional version matters.
research: Official catalogue establishes that Zeus II remains a distinct product. A complete model-specific human delivery evidence dossier was not recovered. II Plus/IV manuals do not validate II’s clinical performance.
fit: No established benefit for the user’s finished serums.
value: Premium delivery value unsupported; no verified eBay quote.

name: ARTISTIC&CO Dr.Arrivo Zeus II PLUS
technology: RF,M/U(MFIP/Ultra Pulse),EMS; compatible essence directions in official manual.
research: Official2026 manual establishes modes and compatible-product handling. No controlled exact-II-Plus matched-product clinical delivery study was recovered. A pulse mechanism is plausible but does not quantify active delivery or visible outcomes.
fit: No reason to enhance prescription retinoids or substitute arbitrary actives for the manual’s compatible medium.
value: Premium purchase not justified by the delivery evidence reviewed; no verified eBay quote.

name: ARTISTIC&CO Dr.Arrivo Zeus IV
technology: MFIP/ULTRA PULSE,EMS,HEAT,LED and app-assisted modes.
research: Official page supports the technology package. No recovered controlled exact-IV study quantifies the incremental clinical benefit of vitamin C,niacinamide,azelaic acid,Thiamidol or tazarotene. “HEAT” is not automatically a conventional RF dose.
fit: A luxury multimode purchase with unestablished added value for this routine.
value: No evidence-based justification for a premium over Medicube/Panasonic for penetration; no verified eBay quote.
